messages.subject: Using remote console on localhost without ssh
messages.subject_clean: Using remote console on localhost without ssh
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

My question may sound dumb, so a word about what I'm trying to accomplish:
I want to run a console connecting to a R interpreter running inside a
docker container.

I tried doing with a remote console.
Setup:

 - in the docker container runs a rmiregistry and a rj console server
running a session called "docker" (launched via the startup.sh script)
 - the 1099 port of the container is bound to the same port on localhost
(as if the registry was running locally

 - I configure a statET remote console:
      * RJ (RMI/JRI) - Manual
      * I do NOT check the ssh Tunneling option
      * whatever I put in the address (docker, //localhost/docker, //
127.0.0.1/docker), it tries to connect via ssh:


in the rj server log (inside docker):
Nov 04, 2014 1:20:39 PM de.walware.rj.server.srvext.ServerAuthMethod
createLogin
INFO: [Auth:fx] creating new login (172.17.42.1).

the a popup appears, asking for login data (rmi:////docker). Whatever I
type, I get a new error popup saying:
Failed to authenticate over SSH connection.


I know I could have it working by running a ssh server inside the
container, but it would add an overhead, and in that case I wonder what is
the "Tunnel connections to R engine through SSH" checkbox used for ??

So my first question is : is-it possible to launch a remote console
directly ?

My second question: would it be possible to create a "regular" Rj console
tthat connects to the R in the docker container ?
I can create a wrapper R script that behaves exactly as a local R
executable, but I do not know how to make a proper R configuration for it
in statET.

Help and advices much appreciated.

Karl Forner

> the a popup appears, asking for login data (rmi:////docker). Whatever I

AUTH="fx:file" and enable AUTH="none".

Regards,
Stephan

messages.subject: StatET Concole Background Color
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone!

StatET does not allow setting R console background color in Eclipse in
my config (see below).

System Config:
Eclipse Platform version 4.3.2.v20140221-1852 (Kepler)
StatET for R version 3.3.2.b20140415
OS: Windows 7

Wouldn't it be great if it were possible to set the background color in
console via the following property sheet path:

Eclipse-->Windows-->Preferences-->StatET-->Run/Debug-->Console-->Output-->BackgroundColor
(which currently does not exist).

I think that installing a close to a hundred-megabyte theme manager just
to manage one simple feature is too much. For some reason this important
feature has been omitted and there is no answer in the Internet.

So so far I've been digging the source code but found no properties that
I could manually change in *.pref (and other files) to make background
of the "nico" (integrated console) dark.

The console background color is always white and it hurts the eyes.

Maybe I missed something and I could modify some file with preferences?
That would be just as good, but a proper property sheet would be better.

Please help me change the console background color.

Thank you in advance,
Alex.

StatET 3.4 (IIRC not yet 3.3) uses the background color of text editors 
also in the console (for input and output).

The background color of text editors is configurable in the preference 
page: General > Editors > Text Editors

Regards,
Stephan

> org.eclipse.core.runtime.CoreException: Downloading file failed: Failed

Setting the environment variable R_DOC_DIR in the startup script to the 
doc directory of R should fix the issue.

>
> But the R help still seems to work pretty well.
>
>
>         Side-questions:
>         I am currently testing using a R inside a docker integrated in
>         StatET
>         via a remote console.
>         Is there a way to connect this R (from the docker) to StatET
>         without a
>         remote console ?
>
>
>     The default R console in StatET requires RJ.
>
>
> Yes, rj is installed in my R installation inside the docker. But how the
> StatET R local console "connects" with a (local) R interpreter ?
> Is it via a shared lib, an executable, other magic ??

It uses the same techniques as the remote console, just local, and 
everything is setup automatically by StatET. So the R interpreter of the 
local R console is started in a separate process and then StatET 
connects to that process.

Regards,
Stephan

messages.subject: "Tasks" in StatET (vs "Tasks" in C)
messages.body_plain:
Hello Stephan and everyone!

Based on my experience with C, when Eclipse detects such a tag as "XXX,"
or "TODO," or "FIXME" in comments to the code, it automatically adds a
task to the Tasks pane.

In StatET, this feature is not automatic (at least in my case). It would
be nice not to have to do recording of Tasks twice: once in the code and
the second time in the "Tasks" pane.

Could you please port this feature from the C IDE plugin?

In any case, thanks in advance.

Regards,
Alex
